text: Fari knew an old song whispered to her grandmother by the spirits of the termite mounds.
In the silver glow of the new moon, she turned three times around an ant hill, stamped her left hoof, and sang three magical words.
In an instant, the coarse gray hide split like a ripe melon.
Fari stepped forth as a tall, radiant maiden with teeth as white as cowrie shells and eyes that sparkled like the river.
Her sisters followed, shedding their bridles to become a court of breathtaking young women, adorned in indigo wrappers and jingling silver anklets.
